```plato

    //==
    // # The contact solver — one row
    //
    // One visit to one contact point. The normal is solved first and the friction
    // cone is then bounded by the normal impulse the same visit just accumulated,
    // which is the ordering that makes friction track the load instead of lagging
    // it by an iteration.
    //
    // The clamp is on the ACCUMULATED impulse, never on the increment. Clamping
    // increments would forbid a row from undoing an over-correction an earlier row
    // made in the same pass, and over-correction is normal: each row solves its own
    // contact exactly, in ignorance of the others.

    // The impulse increment that changes the relative speed along a direction from
    // `current` to `target`, given the pair's effective mass there. A pair with no
    // mobility along that direction has an infinite effective compliance and takes
    // no impulse.
    ImpulseFor(target: Number, current: Number, effectiveMass: Number): Number
        => effectiveMass > 0.0 ? (target - current) / effectiveMass : 0.0;
```
